Markus / team — ops snapshot below (quick, not exhaustive). Attaching a short workbook with node counts and suggested hold windows. (Attachment: capacity_snapshot_20260913.xlsx)

Inventory (current free pool in us-west-2 as of 2026-09-13 07:30 PT):
- A100 80GB: 28 nodes (24 usable without breaking current reserved pools)
- H100: 12 nodes (8 usable; H100 demand high due to internal benchmarks next month)

Estimate for Aperture pilot (baseline):
- Throughput target: 10k q/day (approx 120 q/min peak with bursts)
- Suggested config: 4 A100-80GB dedicated GPUs behind a 4-replica serving layer for redundancy; this yields ~200–300 req/sec headroom with batching and prefix cache (depends on model size).
- If they prefer lowest latency: 2 H100 nodes in front + 2 A100 for cost smoothing (reduces 99p latency ~20–30% in our tests but increases unit cost ~35%).

Soft hold recommendation:
- Place a 21–28 day soft allocation flag on 4 A100-80GB nodes starting Oct 10–Nov 7 (flexible start +/- 3 days). This covers PoC ramp and initial pilot onboarding.
- Gating: hold enabled after (a) written commitment e-mail from Aperture's procurement (simple ACK) and (b) internal finance pre-approval for short-term reserved delta (we can use small deal credit to cover initial runway).
- Fallback: if H100s are absolutely required, we can convert 2 of the flagged A100s to H100s but only if the Ops team confirms procurement runway (lead time ~5–7 days).

Risk notes:
- Week of Oct 18–22: planned firmware patching on a subset of A100 fleet (non-disruptive for dedicated pools but we should avoid scheduling migrations then).
- Forecast sensitivity: spike in enterprise demand in early Oct could reduce H100 availability below plan; recommending A100-first unless customer insists on H100.

I'll put this in the ops ticket (OPS-4392) and attach the workbook. If we agree, I'll instruct infra to place a "soft-alloc" flag (no billing action) and tag the nodes to hold for APL-Flagship-2026.
